tasks.title: Extract shared file-lock helper into src/file-lock.ts
tasks.description: Create src/file-lock.ts and move the cross-process advisory-lock machinery out of src/tasks-file.ts into it: acquireLock(lockPath), the sleepSync(ms) helper, and the LOCK_RETRY_MS / LOCK_MAX_WAIT_MS / LOCK_STALE_MS constants (currently tasks-file.ts:189-240). Export acquireLock and sleepSync. The O_EXCL ('wx') open, stale-lock break via mtimeMs > LOCK_STALE_MS, bounded retry/backoff with jitter, and returning the fd must all be preserved exactly — behavior unchanged. The current lock-timeout error is thrown as a TasksFileError; to avoid file-lock.ts depending on tasks-file.ts, throw a generic Error from the helper (or define a local FileLockError) — update tasks-file.ts accordingly and keep the message text. Refactor mutateTasksFile in tasks-file.ts to import and call the extracted acquireLock. Remove the now-duplicated definitions from tasks-file.ts. TDD: add test/file-lock.test.ts covering acquire→release, that a second acquire on a held lock blocks/retries, and that a stale lockfile (mtime older than LOCK_STALE_MS) is broken — write the test, watch it fail, then implement.
tasks.notes:
# Task #16: Extract shared file-lock helper into src/file-lock.ts

## What was done
- Created `src/file-lock.ts` holding the cross-process advisory-lock machinery moved out of `src/tasks-file.ts` (formerly lines 189–240):
  - `acquireLock(lockPath)` — exported
  - `sleepSync(ms)` — exported
  - `LOCK_RETRY_MS` / `LOCK_MAX_WAIT_MS` / `LOCK_STALE_MS` constants (module-private)
  - `FileLockError` class — exported. Defined locally to avoid file-lock.ts depending on tasks-file.ts. The lock-timeout message text is preserved verbatim ("Could not acquire tasks-file lock at ... within 15000ms; ...").
- Behavior preserved exactly: O_EXCL ('wx') open, best-effort pid/ts metadata write, stale-lock break via `mtimeMs > LOCK_STALE_MS`, bounded retry/backoff with jitter, returns the open fd.
- Refactored `src/tasks-file.ts`: added `import { acquireLock } from './file-lock'`, removed the now-duplicated `sleepSync`/`acquireLock`/constants. `mutateTasksFile` calls the imported `acquireLock` unchanged (signature `acquireLock(lockPath)`).

## Error type change (intentional, per task)
The lock-timeout error was previously thrown as `TasksFileError`; it is now `FileLockError`. Message text is identical. No test or caller asserted on the timeout error *type* (verified via grep of tasks-file.test.ts — only checks lockfile unlink behavior, not error class).

## TDD
Wrote `test/file-lock.test.ts` first and watched it fail (module not found). Tests cover:
1. acquire → release → re-acquire
2. second acquire on a held *fresh* lock blocks/retries until released — uses a real subprocess (`Bun.spawn` running a generated child .ts that imports acquireLock); main holds the lock, asserts the child has not written its sentinel after 400ms, then releases and confirms the child acquires.
3. stale lockfile (mtime set 5 min in the past via `fs.utimesSync`) is broken and re-acquired
4. FileLockError is exported and is an Error subclass with name 'FileLockError'
Also a sleepSync duration sanity check.

## Verification
- `bun test test/file-lock.test.ts test/tasks-file.test.ts` → 23 pass
- `bun test` (full) → 690 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run build` → succeeds (the "not a git repository" line is unrelated build-time version detection noise in a subshell)

tasks.title: Task-counter module src/task-counter.ts
tasks.description: Create src/task-counter.ts owning the monotonic counter persisted at <dataDir>/state.json as { "nextTaskId": N }. Export reserveTaskIds(dataDir: string, count = 1): number[] (returns the contiguous reserved ids) performing an atomic read→increment-by-count→write INSIDE the shared file-lock from src/file-lock.ts (lock on state.json.lock), using the same temp-file-rename atomic write pattern as writeTasksFile in tasks-file.ts. Lazy seeding: when state.json is missing, compute seed = max(all "id" values across <dataDir>/tasks.completed.json + <dataDir>/tasks.json) + 1, floored at 1, and treat that as nextTaskId before reserving. Read ids cheaply (parse JSON, map over tasks[].id); tolerate a missing/empty tasks.completed.json. Export a helper such as seedNextId(dataDir) for reuse by ralph init (task 20). TDD: add test/task-counter.test.ts covering (a) seed-from-archive: archive with max id 15 + empty active → first reserve returns 16; (b) single reserve increments by 1; (c) block reserve count=3 returns 3 contiguous ids and advances the counter by 3; (d) lazy-seed when state.json absent; (e) two sequential reserves never overlap; (f) floor of 1 when no prior ids exist. Write tests first, watch them fail, then implement.

tasks.title: ralph task next-id [--count <n>] CLI command

Write tests first, watch them fail, then implement.

tasks.title: Auto-assign id in ralph task add
tasks.description: Make ralph task add (taskAdd in src/commands/task.ts:218) own id assignment. Inside taskAdd (which has dataDir), call reserveTaskIds(dataDir, 1), inject that id into the parsed payload (overwriting any supplied id — always ignore agent-supplied ids), THEN validate. Because validation runs after injection, the schema's required id is always present, so no schema relaxation is needed. Print the assigned id to stdout (e.g. 'assigned id: <n>') so the agent learns it. Reserve the id only once and reuse it if the mutate retries. Also update the executor prompt in src/commands/run.ts (the DISCOVER AND DOCUMENT block, ~lines 131-133): change it so agents do NOT supply an id — drop id from the 'New tasks need at minimum' list and note the CLI assigns and prints the id. TDD: add tests to test/commands/task.test.ts covering a payload with no id getting a reserved id assigned and appended; a payload WITH an id having it overwritten by the reserved one; and the assigned id being printed to stdout. Write tests first, watch them fail, then implement.

Write tests first, watch them fail, then implement.
